summary: This polymer plant released about 13,600 lb to the air in 2024, almost all methanol, plus a small amount to water.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.where: Within 1 mile: 3,952 residents; Horace Mann Middle School
impacts.how: About 13,600 lb of methanol went out the stack. At high levels methanol can cause headaches and dizziness. Small amounts of maleic anhydride, which can sensitize the lungs, were also released.
avoid: Report strong or unusual odors to the Wisconsin DNR
Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days
Ask the DNR whether the plant's methanol is covered by an air permit

impacts.title: Smog
impacts.how: Methanol helps form ground-level ozone, and Sheboygan's lakeshore doesn't meet the federal ozone standard.
avoid: Plan outdoor exercise for mornings on hot, sunny days
Drive less on ozone action days
Keep rescue inhalers handy on high-ozone days

impacts.title: Sheboygan River
impacts.how: About 15 lb of antimony and zinc reached water. That's small, and these aren't the river's main problem: older PCB pollution is why the DNR still says not to eat resident fish from the lower 14 miles of the river.
avoid: Don't eat resident fish from the lower 14 miles of the Sheboygan River
Follow the DNR fish advisory for other catches
Keep stormwater drains clear of trash and chemicals
